# Contributing

Thanks for being here. Bug reports, questions, and pull requests are all
welcome, and you do not need to be an expert in this project — or in security —
to file something useful.

## Reporting something

Open an issue and pick the template that fits. The templates ask for a few
things up front so we can act without a round-trip; if you cannot answer a
question, leave it blank rather than not filing.

Two things we ask of everyone:

- **Search first.** One duplicate is fine, but a quick look saves us both time.
- **Redact before you paste.** Issues here are public. See
  [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) for what to strip out, and for what to do instead
  when you cannot strip enough.

## What happens to your issue

New issues get an automatic `needs-triage` label. A maintainer will read the
issue, label what kind of issue it is, and either pick it up, put it in the
backlog, or ask you for more detail (`needs-info`).

If we mark something `needs-info` and it goes quiet for a few weeks, we may close
it to keep the queue honest. That is not a judgement on the report — comment any
time and we will reopen it.

## Pull requests

Small, focused pull requests are much easier for us to accept than large ones.

- **For anything non-trivial, open an issue first.** We would rather talk about
  the approach before you spend an evening on it than turn down finished work.
- Typo fixes, docs corrections, and obvious one-line bugs: just send the PR.
- Match the surrounding code's style, and include a test if the project has
  tests for that area.
- Each repository's README documents how to build and test it.

We review PRs on the same board as issues, so the same expectation applies:
normally a few business days.

## Licensing of what you contribute

Ferralon Assay is released under the Apache License 2.0, and contributions come
in under exactly the same terms. Section 5 of that licence says so directly:
unless you explicitly state otherwise, anything you intentionally submit for
inclusion is licensed under Apache-2.0, with no additional terms or conditions
attached.

So that this stays simple for everyone, we need you to be able to say two things
honestly about anything you send:

- **It is yours to give.** You wrote it, or you otherwise hold the right to
  submit it. If you wrote it in the course of work for an employer, make sure
  they are content for you to contribute it.
- **It arrives with no strings.** Do not paste in code that reached you under a
  different licence, and do not attach licence headers, attribution
  requirements, or patent terms of your own. If your change depends on
  third-party code, say so in the pull request and name that code's licence so
  we can check compatibility before merging rather than after.

If you cannot say both of those, open an issue describing the situation instead
of sending the pull request. We would far rather work it out with you up front
than unpick it later.

## Behaviour

Be decent to each other. See [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).
